title: forge env document (forge.dev/env/v1)
description: One forge environment's declaration: the document a KCL env (deploy/kcl/<env>/main.k, `output = forge.render(bundle)`) renders to, or a hand-written env document (deploy/envs/<env>.yaml). Generated from the Go types forge decodes it with. See docs/design/env-document.md.

apiVersion.description: APIVersion names the schema the document conforms to: "forge.dev/env/v1". Required in a hand-written env document; a KCL render omits it (the forge that rendered it is the version).

$schema.description: Schema is the editor hint `$schema`: the URL of this schema. Ignored by forge.

manifests.description: Manifests is the applyable stream: Kubernetes objects, including one forge.dev/v1alpha1 Workload record per cluster-bound workload.

bundled_charts.description: BundledCharts are the HelmCharts delivered in the bundle (delivery = "bundle"), expanded into the apply stream.

generated.description: Generated are the forge.Generated commands whose YAML joins the apply stream.

network_policy.description: NetworkPolicy is the env-wide NetworkPolicy bundle's inputs, or null when the env declares no forge.NetworkPolicy.

statefulset_resize.description: StatefulSetResize tunes the StatefulSet volume-resize Job; present only when declared.

overrides.description: Overrides are Bundle.overrides: per-object patches ("Kind/name" to a patch map) applied to the rendered stream.

config_maps.description: ConfigMaps are Bundle.config_maps as declared. Informational: the objects themselves are in manifests.

runtime_classes.description: RuntimeClasses are Bundle.runtime_classes as declared. Informational: the objects themselves are in manifests.

APIEntity.description: APIEntity is one forge.API: an API the project serves, by its contract.

kind.description: Kind is the contract language: proto or openapi.

spec.description: Spec is the repository-relative contract: the proto directory, or the OpenAPI 3 document.

base_path.description: BasePath is where it is served, starting with "/".

database.description: Database names the declared database it serves from.

AlertRuleEntity.description: AlertRuleEntity is one forge.AlertRule, severity already defaulted.

AlertsEntity.description: AlertsEntity mirrors kcl/schema.k Observability.alerts as render.k projects it.

receivers.description: Receivers are the local stack's (forge.AlertReceiver); a hosted env's receivers live in the control plane.

AnalyticsChannelEntity.description: AnalyticsChannelEntity mirrors kcl/schema.k Channel, conditions already lowercased; at least one of Host, Source and Medium is set.

AnalyticsEntity.description: AnalyticsEntity mirrors kcl/schema.k Analytics. Mode and Dashboards are always set (the schema defaults them); Activation and ActivationWindow are empty when the frontend left them to forge's defaults.

mode.description: Mode is "off" | "aggregate" | "identified" (the default) | "full"; a non-default one reaches the browser as the runtime config's ANALYTICS_MODE.

AnalyticsGoalEntity.description: AnalyticsGoalEntity mirrors kcl/schema.k Goal: exactly one of Event and Route is set.

BucketEntity.description: BucketEntity is one hosted forge.Bucket: the ManagedBucket the hosted provider publishes under Name.

BucketRef.description: BucketRef names a ManagedBucket, in the workload's own namespace, and one connection fact of it to project. Like DatabaseRef it NAMES A BUCKET, NEVER A SECRET, so what it can resolve to is closed by construction.

key.description: Key is the connection fact. Required: unlike a database's uri, no one fact of a bucket is the obvious default.

BucketRuntime.description: BucketRuntime mirrors forge.OnBucket: WHERE the assembled tree goes. The build and assembly inputs (public_dir, base_path, bundle, cache_control) are the frontend's own (FrontendEntity).

keep_releases.description: KeepReleases has NO omitempty, deliberately. 0 is a meaningful value ("retain everything, never prune"), and the KCL renderer projects the key unconditionally so it survives the round trip. An omitempty here would drop it and the provider would read the absent key back as the default 10, pruning archived releases the author explicitly asked forge to keep — in a bucket, where the loss is not recoverable.

BuildContext.description: BuildContext is either a local path / BuildKit reference (a scalar), or a GitSource pin (a mapping). These alternatives cannot silently override one another. Resolution belongs to the CLI; loading config never fetches code.

BuildOnlyDeploy.description: BuildOnlyDeploy is the forge.BuildOnly runtime: the workload is built and shipped as an artifact, never run — a CLI shipped in a release, etc. BuildVariants lets one workload emit several binaries (different ldflags / build tags).

BuildVariant.description: BuildVariant describes one binary produced by a build-only service.

tags.description: BuildTags are the variant's `go build -tags`. The render names them `tags` (kcl/render.k _render_build_variant); this field read `build_tags`, which no render emits, so a variant's tags were dropped until the env schema's fixture check caught the mismatch.

BundleDir.description: BundleDir is one extra pre-built static directory assembled into a published site alongside the frontend's own build output. Dest empty means the site root. Runtime-neutral: every static runtime assembles it the same way.

BundledChartOutput.description: BundledChartOutput is one `output.bundled_charts` entry (a HelmChart whose delivery is "bundle"), in the projection _render_helm_chart emits.

CacheRule.description: CacheRule is one Cache-Control header applied to the objects a glob matches. Order is significant: first match wins.

ClusterEntity.description: ClusterEntity mirrors the kcl/schema.k Cluster — a k3d cluster forge ensures exists before deploying. The reconcile (clusterPhase) reads these and runs `k3d cluster create` for any that are absent.

provider.description: Provider selects which ClusterProvider (see cluster_provider.go) ensures this cluster: "k3d" (default), "vcluster", or "gke". Only "k3d" is implemented — see clusterProviderRegistry.

context.description: Context is the derived kubectl context (`k3d-<name>`), projected so the reconcile / kubeconfig mint can target the cluster without re-deriving the prefix.

image.description: Image pins the k3s node image used for flag-driven clusters. Config-driven clusters declare the image in their authoritative k3d YAML instead.

network.description: Network is the derived docker network this cluster joins — `k3d-<owner.name>` for a secondary, empty for an owner cluster.

registry_inherit.description: RegistryInherit is the derived registry-inherit flag — true when an `owner` is set (forge mirrors the owner's registry onto this cluster's node), false for an owner cluster.

ingress.description: Ingress, when true, installs the Gateway API stack (pinned Gateway-API CRDs + the Envoy Gateway controller via helm + the `eg` GatewayClass) into this cluster after it's ensured. A fresh k3d cluster ships none of these; an env whose Gateway/HTTPRoute/GRPCRoute resources land on this cluster needs it on. Idempotent (helm upgrade --install + kubectl apply).

host_ports.description: HostPorts, when true, merges the generated deploy/k3d-ports.yaml Gateway listener host-port fragment into the k3d config at create time. Ingress IMPLIES this (an imperatively-installed Gateway also needs the host ports). Set HostPorts explicitly when the controller is installed declaratively (Ingress=false) but the cluster still hosts a Gateway whose listeners must be host-mapped at create time.

cluster_cidr.description: ClusterCIDR / ServiceCIDR are the pod and Service address blocks k3s allocates from, reaching `k3d cluster create` as the k3s server args --cluster-cidr / --service-cidr. Empty (the default, and every cluster that does not declare them) leaves k3s on its own defaults — 10.42.0.0/16 pods, 10.43.0.0/16 services — so no argument is added and the created cluster is identical to before.

ClusterRuntime.description: ClusterRuntime is forge.Cluster: a Kubernetes cluster the author operates. Cluster IS the kubectl context. Replicas, ports and probes are not here — they are the workload's spec, the same on every runtime.

ClusterTargetEntity.description: ClusterTargetEntity is the rendered `cluster_target` (kcl/render.k `_render_cluster_target`): the env-wide coordinates a Bundle declares once. Only the fields forge resolves env-wide facts from are read.

connected_cluster.description: ConnectedCluster is the control-plane cluster this target names, by the name `forge cluster connect` registered. Empty for a k3d cluster, which forge applies to directly.

image_pull_secrets.description: ImagePullSecrets are the pull Secrets the target declares. Each cluster workload's runtime carries the list it pulls with (ClusterRuntime), so this env-wide copy is recorded, not read.

ComposeRuntime.description: ComposeRuntime is forge.Compose: the workload is a docker-compose service. Compose owns the container definition, so the workload contributes only its name and this block.

env.description: Env is the map forge puts in the `docker compose` PROCESS environment — where the compose file's own `${VAR}` references interpolate from. Distinct from EnvFile, which only reaches containers.

shared.description: Shared marks the stack as machine infrastructure every worktree of the repo uses; forge drives it from the primary checkout. See OnCompose.shared in kcl/workload.k.

optional.description: Optional marks a service the app does not need in order to run (local observability): `forge env up` skips it, with a warning, when no Docker daemon answers. See OnCompose.optional in kcl/workload.k.

ConfigMapKeyRef.description: ConfigMapKeyRef names one key of a ConfigMap in the workload's own namespace.

ConfigMapVolumeSource.description: ConfigMapVolumeSource names a ConfigMap, and optionally which keys to project.

items.description: Items selects keys and their file paths. Unset projects every key as a file named after it. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:MaxItems=64

Container.description: Container is a sidecar: a second container in the workload's pod.

name.description: Name is the container name, unique within the pod. It must not equal the workload's own name, which the main container uses. +kubebuilder:validation:MinLength=1 +kubebuilder:validation:MaxLength=63 +kubebuilder:validation:Pattern=`^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$`

image.description: Image is the sidecar's image, typically third-party (gcr.io/cloud-sql-connectors/cloud-sql-proxy:2.14.1). +kubebuilder:validation:MinLength=1 +kubebuilder:validation:MaxLength=500

env.description: Env is the sidecar's environment. Like WorkloadSpec.Env, it has no portable entry-count limit; exec byte limits depend on resolved values. +optional +listType=map +listMapKey=name

ports.description: Ports are the sidecar's container ports. +optional +listType=map +listMapKey=name +kubebuilder:validation:MaxItems=16

resources.description: Resources is the sidecar's compute request and limit, with the same defaults as the main container. +optional

probes.description: Probes are the sidecar's own probes. Unset means none: unlike a service, a sidecar gets no implicit TCP probe. +optional

native.description: Native renders the sidecar as a Kubernetes native sidecar: an initContainer with restartPolicy Always (GA in Kubernetes 1.29). The kubelet starts it BEFORE the main container and waits for its startup probe to pass, and stops it AFTER the main container exits. A plain sidecar starts concurrently with the main container, so a main process that dials the sidecar at boot (a database proxy on 127.0.0.1) races it and fails until the sidecar is listening. Set Probes.StartupPath so "started" means "ready to serve"; without a startup probe the kubelet only waits for the process to launch. +optional

ControlPlaneEntity.description: ControlPlaneEntity is the parsed bundle-level hosted control-plane declaration (kcl/schema.k ControlPlane): WHICH endpoint this env talks to, and the NAME of the env var its bearer credential is read from.

registry_host.description: RegistryHost is the platform registry this org's artifacts live on, defaulted in KCL to forge.RELIANT_REGISTRY_HOST.

claimable.description: Claimable declares the env an ANONYMOUS deploy (`forge env deploy <env> --claimable`): it is judged under the claimable plan (deploy.HostedPlanClaimable) by every preview and check, and a signed-in deploy of it is refused until the declaration is removed.

ControlPlaneSecretEntity.description: ControlPlaneSecretEntity mirrors the kcl/schema.k ControlPlaneSecret — a Secret the env's declared control plane supplies and renews. It carries a destination and a kind, never a value.

type.description: Type is the render's record tag, "control_plane_secret".

cluster.description: Cluster is the kube context it lands in; ConnectedCluster is the name `forge cluster connect` registered, the credential it is delivered with.

kind.description: Kind says what the control plane mints into it ("telemetry_token", "identity", "identity_machine_key", "identity_jwks").

keys.description: Keys are the data keys the control plane writes.

required.description: Required is true when a workload reads the Secret without an optional marker, so its pods wait for the first delivery.

delivery.description: Delivery is release.ControlPlaneSecretDeliveryStore when the control plane writes the store and ESO delivers the Secret; Source is then the floating store source ESO reads.

DNSRecordEntity.description: DNSRecordEntity mirrors the kcl/schema.k DNSRecord — a DNS record a deploy depends on. forge can't authoritatively verify external DNS, so this is a render-time checklist entry (and a `--check` note), not a hard block. Target is the expected value (LB IP / CNAME target) when known.

target.description: Target is the expected value (LB IP for A/AAAA, CNAME target). Often unknown at author time (ephemeral LB IP), so optional.

DatabaseDashboards.description: DatabaseDashboards is the opt-in dashboard role and the limits its queries run under. The limits are enforced by whoever queries as the role (the control plane, pkg/dbquery); the role itself is bounded by Postgres: the column SELECTs the project's migrations grant it (and nothing but read privileges, which the migrator enforces), a connection limit, and a read-only transaction. See pkg/dbgrants.

enabled.description: Enabled lets the dashboard role log in. False renders it NOLOGIN. +optional

rowCap.description: RowCap is the most rows one panel query returns. +optional +kubebuilder:default=1000 +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=1 +kubebuilder:validation:Maximum=10000

timeoutMs.description: TimeoutMs is the statement timeout of one panel query, in milliseconds. +optional +kubebuilder:default=5000 +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=100 +kubebuilder:validation:Maximum=10000

maxConcurrency.description: MaxConcurrency is how many panel queries run at once. The role's connection limit is one more than this, so a query that is being cancelled never starves the next. +optional +kubebuilder:default=2 +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=1 +kubebuilder:validation:Maximum=4

DatabaseEntity.description: DatabaseEntity is one managed database: its name (the CloudNativePG Cluster name), its runtime ("cluster" or "hosted"), where it lands when cluster-bound, and its spec, which is forge's Go tier type.

dialect.description: Dialect is the database's SQL dialect: postgres.

migrations.description: Migrations is where its migrations live and which tool applies them.

orm.description: ORM places its generated data layer.

DatabaseMigrationSafetyEntity.description: DatabaseMigrationSafetyEntity is forge.DatabaseMigrationSafety: the migration-safety lint's dials for one database.

DatabaseMigrationsEntity.description: DatabaseMigrationsEntity is forge.DatabaseMigrations: forge.yaml's `database.migrations:` block, declared per database (Driver is its `tool`).

dir.description: Dir is the repository-relative directory holding the migrations.

driver.description: Driver is the tool that applies them: forge, golang-migrate, goose, atlas, flyway, dbmate or custom.

apply.description: Apply, Status and Check are argv (no shell) overriding a built-in driver's; see config.MigrationsConfig.

DatabaseORMEntity.description: DatabaseORMEntity is forge.DatabaseORM: the repository-relative package directory the database's ORM projects into.

DatabaseRef.description: DatabaseRef names a ManagedDatabase, in the workload's own namespace, whose credential to project.

key.description: Key is the credential part. Empty means uri. +optional

DatabaseRestore.description: DatabaseRestore is a declarative recovery: which database's backups to read, and optionally how far to replay them.

sourceDatabase.description: SourceDatabase is the ManagedDatabase whose backups are read. It may be this database's own name (recreating it in place) or another in the same environment — never one in another environment, which the platform enforces by scoping the object-store prefix, not by checking a string here. +kubebuilder:validation:MinLength=1

pointInTime.description: PointInTime stops recovery at an RFC3339 timestamp instead of replaying every archived WAL. Unset recovers as far as the archive goes.

DockerBuild.description: DockerBuild mirrors the kcl/schema.k DockerBuild — the per-service container image build. Reuses forge's existing docker primitives (tag/registry/push/build-contexts) as behavior; these fields select the dockerfile/platform/target/build_args.

context.description: Context is the MAIN `docker build` context directory, relative to the project root. Empty is the project root ("."), so an unset Context builds byte-identically to before this field existed. Distinct from BuildContexts, which are NAMED --build-context entries. The Dockerfile need not live under it — docker allows -f outside the context.

build_contexts.description: BuildContexts maps a `docker buildx --build-context name=value` entry THIS service's Dockerfile needs (a sibling-checkout path the Dockerfile `COPY --from=name`s, a `docker-image://` override, …). Same value shapes as config.DockerConfig.BuildContexts. Empty falls back to the project-level forge.yaml docker.build_contexts.

sizeLimitBytes.description: SizeLimitBytes caps the volume. Unset means no cap beyond the node's ephemeral storage. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=1

EnvVar.description: EnvVar is one container environment variable.

secretRef.description: SecretRef projects one key of a Secret in the workload's namespace. +optional

managedSecret.description: ManagedSecret names a value in the environment's secret store, and whether its absence is tolerated. +optional

bucketRef.description: BucketRef projects one connection fact of a ManagedBucket, read from the Secret the platform writes for it (BucketCredentialSecretName). +optional

workloadURL.description: WorkloadURL is the public URL of another workload in the SAME environment — the canonical case is a backend's CORS_ORIGINS naming the StaticSite that calls it. It names a workload, never a hostname, so it follows the workload when its URL changes.

configMapRef.description: ConfigMapRef projects one key of a ConfigMap in the workload's namespace. Full profile only. +optional

fieldRef.description: FieldRef projects a pod field through the Downward API (valueFrom.fieldRef.fieldPath). Full profile only. +optional

ExternalDatabaseEntity.description: ExternalDatabaseEntity is one forge.ExternalDatabase: a Postgres forge does not run, reached through Service in Namespace on Cluster (a kube context), signed in to as Username with the password at PasswordKey of the PasswordSecret Secret in that namespace.

reach.description: Reach is how a control plane dials it: "port_forward" (the default, through the kube API) or "direct" (<service>.<namespace>.svc:<port> from inside the cluster). forge db query always port-forwards.

port.description: Port is the Service port, 0 when undeclared.

dialect.description: Dialect is the database's SQL dialect: postgres.

migrations.description: Migrations is where its migrations live and which tool applies them.

orm.description: ORM places its generated data layer.

ExternalRuntime.description: ExternalRuntime is forge.OnExternal as rendered (kcl/render.k _render_runtime). An unset hook is nil.

env.description: Env is extra environment for every hook; FORGE_* is forge's.

pass_env.description: PassEnv hands the hooks the workload's resolved env as well.

working_dir.description: WorkingDir is where hooks run, relative to the project root.

timeout.description: Timeout is the per-hook ceiling in seconds; 0 = the default.

platform.description: Platform is the GOARCH the image runs on (OnExternal.platform), which forge builds for. "" = amd64, the KCL default.

ExternalSecretEntity.description: ExternalSecretEntity mirrors the kcl/schema.k ExternalSecret — an out-of-band Secret a deploy DEPENDS ON but forge does NOT create. forge reads these to print a render-time prerequisite checklist and to drive the deploy preflight (a declared-required-but-absent Secret/key BLOCKS, reusing the same SecretGetter as the secretKeyRef preflight). ValueGroup, when set, ties this Secret to others that must carry the SAME logical value (the cross-secret byte-match group).

type.description: Type is the render's record tag, "secret".

reason.description: Reason is a short human note: why the deploy needs this Secret. Shown in the checklist so the operator knows what breaks if it's absent.

value_group.description: ValueGroup is the shared id tying this Secret to other ExternalSecrets that must carry the same logical value (cross-secret byte-match). Empty => a standalone prereq (no byte-match group).

clusters.description: Clusters are the kubectl contexts the Secret is declared to be required on (ExternalSecret.clusters). Empty => the preflight infers them from the clusters that consume its namespace (scopeRequiredSecretsToClusters).

source.description: Source is the rendered forge.StoreSource: nil for a Secret something else provisions, set for one ESO syncs from a store.

FieldRef.description: FieldRef selects a pod field for the Downward API. Only the path is modelled. apiVersion is always v1 for the fields a container env can read, so a knob for it would be a field that is either redundant or wrong.

fieldPath.description: FieldPath is the pod field, e.g. metadata.name or status.podIP. +kubebuilder:validation:MinLength=1 +kubebuilder:validation:MaxLength=253

spa_fallback.description: SPAFallback is the entry document served for client-side routes ("/index.html"); empty means no SPA fallback.

keep_asset_releases.description: KeepAssetReleases is how many releases' hashed assets the live site serves. The render projects it unconditionally (default 10, floor 2).

FlowCheckEntity.description: FlowCheckEntity mirrors the kcl/workload.k FlowCheck: one app-flow health endpoint a workload serves. Path is the only required field; the URL is resolved at smoke time (see resolveFlowChecks), never declared.

FluxDeliveryControl.description: FluxDeliveryControl is one delivery-policy control on a self-hosted delivery: the mode the env asks for and the mode in effect.

FluxDeliveryEntity.description: FluxDeliveryEntity is the resolved self-hosted delivery of an `applier = "flux"` env, as kcl/render.k's _render_flux_delivery projects it.

chart.description: Chart is the bootstrap platform chart's name (fluxdelivery.ChartName).

env.description: Env and Cluster are the env and the one kubectl context it targets: where its Flux runs and every tree applies.

namespace.description: Namespace is the env's delivery namespace; ResourceSet the delivery ResourceSet's name in it.

apply_identities.description: ApplyIdentities: every tree applies as a derived identity. False: kustomize-controller applies as itself and no identity is derived.

delivery_scope.description: DeliveryScope is "namespace" or "cluster": where the rollout/post identity may write.

pull_secret_from.description: PullSecretFrom is `<namespace>/<name>` of the image-pull Secret the bootstrap copies into Namespace as PullSecret; both empty when the registry needs no credential.

signing.description: Signing and FluxVerify are delivery_policy's controls as asked and as they take effect here (at most audit).

registry.description: Registry is FluxDelivery.registry as declared: the registry subtree the env's bundles are pushed to, as this machine reaches it. Empty: the registry of the env's first cluster workload image (fluxRegistryBase).

FrontendConfigEntity.description: FrontendConfigEntity mirrors the kcl/schema.k FrontendConfig — the typed, well-known frontend knobs forge maps to framework-specific env var names (NEXT_PUBLIC_* / VITE_* / EXPO_PUBLIC_*, plus Next.js's NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED) and enforces on the build path. Mock is the load-bearing knob: "off" (default) | "true" | "hybrid". See frontendConfigEnv for the field→variable mapping and the build-path mock force in deploy.go.

FrontendEntity.description: FrontendEntity is one frontend from rendered KCL: a dev server, or a static build forge publishes. Runtime says which (ADR 0002 §6), and every consumer dispatches on Runtime.Type. The static build facts (PublicDir, BasePath, Bundle, CacheControl) are the frontend's own, identical on every runtime that publishes a build.

path.description: Path is the frontend's directory in THIS repository. Empty exactly when Source is set — a cross-repo frontend has no directory here until the source resolver materializes one.

source.description: Source pins the frontend's code to another repository at a ref (kcl/schema.k GitSource). nil for the ordinary in-repo frontend. Callers that shell into a frontend must resolve this to a directory via internal/gitsource rather than reading Path — see resolveFrontendEntitySources.

config.description: Config is the typed, well-known knobs block (kcl/schema.k FrontendConfig). nil when the frontend declares no `config`. forge expands it into the SAME env stream as EnvVars via frontendConfigEnv, with explicit EnvVars winning on a variable collision. See EffectiveEnvVars.

telemetry.description: Telemetry is the browser telemetry the frontend declares beyond the env's observability signals (kcl/schema.k BrowserTelemetry). nil when it declares none.

routes.description: Routes is the CRUD-page allowlist (kcl/schema.k Frontend.routes): route slugs, or the single value "none". Empty means every CRUD entity.

runtime.description: Runtime is where the frontend runs. Always present in a render: the Bundle refuses a frontend with none. Zero only for a frontend bridged in from forge.yaml (mergeConfigFrontends), which is dev-served.

image.description: Image is where an OnHosted frontend's site release is pushed: the reference the frontend DECLARES, registry host included. Empty for every other runtime (the render refuses it there, and requires it on hosted). forge appends the platform's static.v1 layout — see deploytarget.HostedStaticRepository — so the declared reference stays exactly what the author wrote.

public_dir.description: PublicDir is the build's static output dir relative to the frontend's code — declared, else the type's convention (resolved by the render).

asset_dir.description: AssetDir is the build's content-hashed asset directory relative to PublicDir — declared, else the type's convention ("assets" for vite, "_next/static" for nextjs). Empty when the build has none.

base_path.description: BasePath mounts the frontend under a sub-path ("/admin"); empty is the site root.

bundle.description: Bundle is the extra pre-built static dirs assembled into the site.

cache_control.description: CacheControl is the ordered Cache-Control rules forge applies where it publishes the build itself (OnBucket object headers, OnFirebase firebase.json headers; the render refuses them elsewhere).

runtime_config.description: RuntimeConfig is the frontend's declared `runtime_config` RESOLVED to literals by the KCL render (forge.WorkloadURL references lowered to the target's URL). It is layered over the typed per-env config when forge writes config.js. EMPTY on a hosted env, where the control plane resolves references and writes the document itself.

runtime_config_spec.description: RuntimeConfigSpec is the same declaration in the StaticSite spec's wire shape, references KEPT. The hosted provider publishes it as spec.runtimeConfig.

sourcemaps.description: Sourcemaps is "publish" (the default when empty), "public" or "off": whether the built source maps leave the served tree for a sidecar, are served, or are dropped. See deploytarget.Sourcemaps*.

FrontendRuntime.description: FrontendRuntime is a frontend's resolved runtime. Type carries the tag; Bucket / Firebase are non-nil exactly when Type names them. host, hosted and build-only carry no fields on a frontend.

replay.description: Replay is the frontend's session replay switch (BrowserTelemetry.replay). It reaches the browser as runtime config (OTEL_REPLAY) and the env's policy as the replay opt-in.

service_name.description: ServiceName is the service.name a sourced frontend's SDK reports, as declared (BrowserTelemetry.service_name). Empty for an in-repo frontend.

analytics.description: Analytics is the frontend's declared product analytics (BrowserTelemetry.analytics); nil when it declares none.

FunnelEntity.description: FunnelEntity mirrors kcl/schema.k Funnel, window and by already defaulted.

step_filters.description: StepFilters are the forge.Step refinements, one per step (an empty one for a bare name); nil when every step is a bare name.

FunnelStepEntity.description: FunnelStepEntity mirrors what kcl/schema.k Step adds to its event name.

GRPCRouteEntity.description: GRPCRouteEntity mirrors the kcl/schema.k GRPCRoute. Shape matches HTTPRouteEntity — the distinction is the rendered Gateway API resource kind (GRPCRoute vs HTTPRoute).

GatewayAddressEntity.description: GatewayAddressEntity mirrors the kcl/schema.k GatewayAddress — one entry in the Gateway's spec.addresses, pinning it to a load-balancer address. Type is "NamedAddress" (Value is a GKE reserved static-IP reservation name) or "IPAddress" (Value is a literal IP).

GatewayEntity.description: GatewayEntity mirrors the kcl/schema.k Gateway. Listeners are inlined. Tls is nil when the gateway is plaintext.

GatewayListenerEntity.description: GatewayListenerEntity mirrors the kcl/schema.k GatewayListener. Protocol is "HTTP" | "HTTPS" | "H2C".

GatewayTLSEntity.description: GatewayTLSEntity is the TLS block on a Gateway. Mode selects the cert origin: "cert_manager" (default — cert-manager Certificate emitted alongside the Gateway, CertIssuer names a ClusterIssuer), "mkcert" (Secret populated host-side by `forge cluster up` via the mkcert binary; CertIssuer unused), or "gke_certmap" (GCP Certificate Manager map named by Certmap terminates TLS; CertIssuer / SecretName unused — the GKE Gateway controller binds the map via the `networking.gke.io/certmap` annotation forge stamps on the Gateway).

GenerateSpec.description: GenerateSpec mirrors KCL's forge.GeneratedSecret: how to mint a store value that is pure random key material.

GeneratedOutput.description: GeneratedOutput is one `output.generated` entry (forge.Generated): a command whose stdout is Kubernetes YAML forge joins to the apply stream.

GitSource.description: GitSource declares a component's code as "that repository at that ref" rather than a directory that must already exist on disk.

repo.description: Repo is the repository: host/owner/name ("github.com/reliant-labs/reliant"), which forge expands to an https clone URL, or an explicit https://, ssh://, or git@host:owner/name URL, which is used verbatim.

ref.description: Ref is the tag, branch, or commit sha to check out. Required — forge does not default to a repository's default branch, because an unpinned dependency is precisely the problem this type solves.

subdir.description: Subdir is the path within the repository holding this component's source ("web"). Empty means the repository root.

GoBuild.description: GoBuild mirrors the kcl/schema.k GoBuild. Cmd is the go-build target package (e.g. "./cmd/trader"); the rest are the cross-compile + flag knobs build.go passes straight to `go build`.

traffic.description: Traffic is the typed per-route policy; nil when the route declares none. It replaced a `raw_policy` string that nothing in forge ever emitted (ADR-0003 F2).

HelmChartEntity.description: HelmChartEntity is one declared platform dependency from rendered KCL (the `output.helm_charts` projection of forge.HelmChart). It is the declaration only — forge expands it via `helm template --skip-crds` Go-side (internal/cluster.RenderHelmChart) and folds the manifests into the apply stream, selected by `--target=<name>`. helm is a RENDERER, not an installer: there is no release, no `helm install`.

chart.description: Chart is the chart name for a repo chart; empty for an OCI chart.

repo.description: Repo is the chart-repo URL; mutually exclusive with OCI.

oci.description: OCI is the OCI chart ref; mutually exclusive with Repo.

version.description: Version is the pinned chart version.

namespace.description: Namespace is the namespace the chart renders into (helm template -n).

values.description: Values is the helm values overlay, passed through verbatim.

crds.description: CRDs selects which forge-owned CRD bundle to apply FIRST (Established-gated) before the chart's controllers: "" (none), "gateway-api", "cert-manager" or "external-secrets". The chart is rendered --skip-crds, so forge owns the CRD surface.

cluster.description: Cluster is the kubectl CONTEXT this chart installs into, overriding the env's primary cluster for this chart alone. The KCL `cluster` field is a forge.Cluster REFERENCE and the render projects its derived `.context` (`k3d-<name>`) here, so the value is always the context forge applies with and can never drift from the cluster the declaration names. Empty => the env's primary cluster.

cluster_target.description: ClusterTarget is true when Cluster came from a forge.ClusterTarget (a cluster you operate) rather than a forge.Cluster. A target is its own declaration, so validateChartCluster does not look for it in the env's k3d clusters.

manifests.description: Manifests are consumer-declared raw k8s manifest dicts that ride this chart's `--target` (the `eg` GatewayClass, cert-manager ClusterIssuers) — the cluster-scoped instances the chart's controller reconciles but the chart itself doesn't ship. Stamped with the chart's app-label and applied AFTER its controllers; excluded from a bare app deploy.

namespace_labels.description: NamespaceLabels / NamespaceAnnotations are written onto the Namespace forge creates for the chart (e.g. Pod Security Admission labels).

prune.description: Prune says whether a re-apply deletes the chart's objects that left the render. A pointer so a contract that omits it (an older render) reads as the schema default, true, rather than as false.

patches.description: Patches are merge patches for the objects the chart renders, keyed `Kind/name` (see cluster.HelmChartSpec.Patches).

HostInfraEntity.description: HostInfraEntity is one `Bundle.infra` entry: a third-party server forge runs as a HOST PROCESS instead of a container — the default shape for dev infrastructure on a machine that cannot afford a container runtime. See internal/hostinfra for the supervisor and internal/deploytarget.HostInfraProvider for the dispatch.

idp_database.description: engine = "zitadel" only — the dev IdP's backing database and its declarative bootstrap. See the HostInfra schema in kcl/schema.k.

HostRuntime.description: HostRuntime is forge.Host: run the workload as a local process. The argv is NOT declared here — hostlaunch.BuildCmd derives it from the runner, the workload's build and its args. Env comes from the workload's spec.env.

working_dir.description: WorkingDir overrides the launched subprocess's working directory. Relative paths resolve against the project root. Use this for cross-repo binaries whose runner config (e.g. Air's build_cmd paths) resolves relative to a sibling repo. Default: project root.

listen_ports.description: ListenPorts are the host TCP ports this workload itself BINDS. When declared, the `forge env up` port-conflict pre-flight and readiness gate check EXACTLY these; otherwise the workload's declared spec.ports stand in.

startup_after.description: StartupAfter names host workloads or frontend dev servers that env up must observe ready before launching this workload. Empty preserves order.

HostedRuntime.description: HostedRuntime is forge.OnHosted. The control plane owns every placement fact except the node architecture, which forge needs to build the image.

KCLEnvVar.description: KCLEnvVar is a single env var entry from the rendered KCL. Distinct type so we don't pull in the project-config EnvVar (which carries codegen-specific fields the KCL renderer doesn't know about).

secret_optional.description: SecretOptional exempts this var's secret_ref from the store pre-flight. Set by config codegen from `optional: true` on a `sensitive` proto field — never hand-authored.

KeyToPath.description: KeyToPath projects one key to a file path relative to the mount.

path.description: Path is RELATIVE to the mount and may not contain "..", so a key can never be written outside the volume. +kubebuilder:validation:MinLength=1 +kubebuilder:validation:MaxLength=4096

KubeconfigPolicyRuleEntity.description: KubeconfigPolicyRuleEntity mirrors kcl/schema.k's KubeconfigPolicyRule — one rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 PolicyRule.

resource_names.description: ResourceNames limits the rule to these named objects. Empty means every object of Resources.

KubeconfigSecretEntity.description: KubeconfigSecretEntity mirrors the kcl/schema.k KubeconfigSecret — a cross-cluster kubeconfig forge mints FRESH each up and stores as a k8s Secret. The mint step (mintKubeconfigSecrets) resolves the target's endpoint at runtime and never persists the IP.

target_context.description: TargetContext is the kubectl context addressing the target cluster. Empty means the k3d derivation (`k3d-<TargetCluster>`, resolved via `k3d kubeconfig get`). Set, it names a context in the operator's own kubeconfig — which is how a non-k3d cluster (GKE) becomes addressable at all.

service_account.description: ServiceAccount, when non-nil, switches the mint from COPYING the operator's credential to MINTING one on the target. See KubeconfigServiceAccountEntity.

KubeconfigServiceAccountEntity.description: KubeconfigServiceAccountEntity mirrors kcl/schema.k's KubeconfigServiceAccount — the ServiceAccount + RBAC + long-lived token forge converges ON THE TARGET cluster so the minted kubeconfig carries a credential a POD can present.

namespaces.description: Namespaces, when non-empty, binds Rules as a Role in each listed namespace instead of one cluster-wide ClusterRole.

ManagedBucketSpec.description: ManagedBucketSpec is an object-storage bucket the hosted platform provisions for one environment: a forge.Bucket bound to forge.OnHosted.

publicRead.description: PublicRead makes every object readable without a signature (avatars, a public gallery). Off, objects are reached only through presigned URLs, and the bucket's public access prevention stays enforced. +optional

corsOrigins.description: CORSOrigins are the browser origins that upload to and download from the bucket directly, each scheme://host[:port] or "*". The platform ADDS the environment's own hosted frontend origins and bound custom domains, so an author never lists their own app here. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:MaxItems=32 +listType=set

deletionPolicy.description: DeletionPolicy is what deleting this resource does to the objects. Default retain, for the reason DeletionPolicy states: deleting a declaration says nothing about whether the uploads should exist. +optional +kubebuilder:default=retain

ManagedDatabaseSpec.description: ManagedDatabaseSpec is a dedicated Postgres, rendered as a CloudNativePG Cluster in the workload's own namespace.

engine.description: Engine is the database engine. Default postgres. +optional +kubebuilder:default=postgres

instances.description: Instances is how many Postgres instances run: one primary plus (Instances-1) hot standbys. Default 1, ceiling MaxDatabaseInstances. A standby buys failover, not durability. +optional +kubebuilder:default=1 +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=1 +kubebuilder:validation:Maximum=3

storageGiB.description: StorageGiB sizes EACH instance's volume, so the cluster provisions Instances × StorageGiB. Default DefaultDatabaseStorageGiB. +optional +kubebuilder:default=10 +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=1 +kubebuilder:validation:Maximum=500

deletionPolicy.description: DeletionPolicy is what deleting this resource does to the data. Default retain. +optional +kubebuilder:default=retain

restore.description: Restore, when set, bootstraps this database from a backup instead of from an empty initdb. DECLARING it is the whole restore procedure: there is no imperative RPC, because a restore that only exists as a command is one nobody can review, repeat, or run at 3am from a git revert.

dashboards.description: Dashboards opts the database into live dashboard panels: it lets the dashboard role (forge_dash) log in. The role reads only what the project's migrations GRANT it. Nil means disabled, and a disabled database renders the role NOLOGIN with no password, so declaring nothing never leaves a login behind. +optional

ManagedSecretRef.description: ManagedSecretRef names one value in the environment's secret store.

name.description: Name is the secret's logical name. A BARE LOGICAL NAME: env-var shaped, with no separator to traverse, carrying no customer or environment component, so no spelling of it reaches another customer's value. +kubebuilder:validation:MinLength=1 +kubebuilder:validation:MaxLength=253 +kubebuilder:validation:Pattern=`^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`

optional.description: Optional tolerates the store having no value: the materializer skips the name, and the pod starts without the variable. Default false: a missing value fails the materialization and nothing starts. +optional

NetworkPolicyOutput.description: NetworkPolicyOutput is `output.network_policy`: the inputs of the env-wide NetworkPolicy bundle (forge.NetworkPolicy). null when the env declares none.

egress_ports.description: EgressPorts are the external TCP ports every workload may dial.

telemetry_namespace.description: TelemetryNamespace is where the telemetry agent runs ("" for none).

ingress_namespace.description: IngressNamespace is where the ingress controller runs ("" for none).

token_secret.description: TokenSecret is a bearer token the node agent re-reads from a mounted file.

token_from_control_plane.description: TokenFromControlPlane is true when the token is the one the control plane delivers (a ControlPlaneSecret forge declared); TokenSecret then names where it lands.

ObservabilityEntity.description: ObservabilityEntity is the env's typed observability declaration (Bundle.observability) as `output.observability`. Nil when the env declares none: telemetry is off and nothing is injected.

dev_telemetry.description: DevTelemetry is where a LOCAL stack's telemetry is stored: "auto" (the schema default), "hosted" or "local". "" from a render that predates the field, which reads as "auto".

profiles_endpoint.description: ProfilesEndpoint is the full URL of the local profiles collector host processes push to; "" when profiles are off or go to a destination.

alertmanager_port.description: AlertmanagerPort and AlertsPort are the local alerting loop's loopback ports: the compose Alertmanager's and the evaluator's (its in-app sink). Zero when the env runs no local loop (no ports declared, or a destination instead of the local ClickStack).

policy.description: Policy is the resolved opt-out, recorded in the release shape.

alerts.description: Alerts is Observability.alerts as the author declared it; nil when none.

analytics.description: Analytics is Observability.analytics, the project's Events funnels and counts; nil when none.

ObservabilityPolicyEntity.description: ObservabilityPolicyEntity is Observability's resolved opt-out: Disabled names the categories (traces, metrics, logs, profiles, metadata, browser) the author switched off, every one when Enabled is false.

opt_in.description: OptIn names the default-off categories the env turned on (replay).

OpenBaoBootstrapEntity.description: OpenBaoBootstrapEntity is the resolved Secret Manager delivery: the Google identities it runs as, and which secrets it moves. Declarations only.

namespace.description: Namespace is the store's, where both service accounts live.

OpenBaoEntity.description: OpenBaoEntity is the rendered `openbao` block (kcl/lib/openbao.k): where the store is and how a client logs in to it. Declarations only; no value.

cluster.description: Cluster is the kube context the store runs in; ConnectedCluster is the name `forge cluster connect` registered.

self_cluster.description: SelfCluster is the store's own cluster id: its auth mount is jwt-<id>.

audience.description: Audience is what the cluster's tokens must carry to log in.

bootstrap_names.description: BootstrapNames are the BootstrapSecret names the component declares that a person may import (the seal key, the Postgres password and the recovery escrow).

bootstrap_generate.description: BootstrapGenerate are the BootstrapSecrets (by secret id) the deploy mints when the bootstrap source has none: only under a GCPSecretManager source, and only the seal key and the Postgres password.

bootstrap.description: Bootstrap is the delivery the component renders under a GCPSecretManager source: nil under any other.

warnings.description: Warnings are the render's notes about the component's configuration (the recovery escrow, kcl/lib/openbao.k), shown with the render.

PVCVolumeSource.description: PVCVolumeSource names an existing PersistentVolumeClaim in the workload's namespace.

PodSecurity.description: PodSecurity is the closed set of pod-identity knobs forge lets a workload change. Each unset field keeps forge's default (uid/gid 65532, fsGroup only when a volume needs it, a read-only root filesystem). The overrides apply to the pod AND to every container forge renders in it (main, sidecar, gating initContainer), so the pod has one identity.

runAsUser.description: RunAsUser is the uid every container runs as. Must not be 0: runAsNonRoot is always true. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=1

runAsGroup.description: RunAsGroup is the primary gid. Must not be 0. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=1

fsGroup.description: FSGroup owns mounted volumes. Must not be 0. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=1

readOnlyRootFilesystem.description: ReadOnlyRootFilesystem false gives the containers a writable root filesystem. Default true. +optional

PolicyRule.description: PolicyRule is one RBAC rule: verbs on resources in API groups.

apiGroups.description: APIGroups are the API groups; "" is the core group. +kubebuilder:validation:MinItems=1

resources.description: Resources are the resource names (plural, lowercase), optionally with a subresource ("pods/log"). +kubebuilder:validation:MinItems=1

verbs.description: Verbs are the allowed verbs, or "*". +kubebuilder:validation:MinItems=1

resourceNames.description: ResourceNames narrows the rule to named objects. +optional

Port.description: Port is one named port a workload listens on.

name.description: Name is the port's name, referenced by Services and probes. An IANA_SVC_NAME, as Kubernetes requires of a container port name: at most 15 characters, lowercase alphanumerics and '-'. +kubebuilder:validation:MinLength=1 +kubebuilder:validation:MaxLength=15 +kubebuilder:validation:Pattern=`^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$`

port.description: Port is the container port number. +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=1 +kubebuilder:validation:Maximum=65535

protocol.description: Protocol is the transport. Default tcp. +optional +kubebuilder:default=tcp

appProtocol.description: AppProtocol is the application protocol the port speaks (h2c, grpc, http, https, ws), set as the Service port's appProtocol so a gateway or mesh can route it correctly. It changes no pod behaviour. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:MaxLength=63 +kubebuilder:validation:Pattern=`^([a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*/)?[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9.]*[a-z0-9])?$`

expose.description: Expose asks the environment to route a PUBLIC hostname to this port: the gateway when self-hosted, the platform's allocated hostname on hosted. Only a service can expose a port, because only a service has a Service object to route to. At most one port per workload is exposed, because status reports one hostname. +optional

domains.description: Domains are CUSTOM hostnames served IN ADDITION to the default hostname. They are only meaningful on the exposed port. The default hostname needs no declaration: hosted allocates a collision-safe one and self-hosted derives one from the env's gateway, so a public workload never has to invent a domain. Hosted verifies ownership of a custom domain before serving it, because on shared infrastructure an unverified hostname is a takeover vector. Self-hosted trusts it. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:MaxItems=8

Probes.description: Probes are a workload's readiness and liveness probes, declared ONCE.

port.description: Port is the container port probed. Unset means the port named http, or the first declared port (see WorkloadSpec.ProbePort). +optional +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=1 +kubebuilder:validation:Maximum=65535

readinessPath.description: ReadinessPath is the HTTP readiness path. Unset means /readyz. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:MaxLength=2048 +kubebuilder:validation:Pattern=`^/.*$`

livenessPath.description: LivenessPath is the HTTP liveness path. Unset means /healthz. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:MaxLength=2048 +kubebuilder:validation:Pattern=`^/.*$`

startupPath.description: StartupPath is the HTTP startup-probe path. Unset means no startup probe. The kubelet holds off readiness and liveness until it passes, and a NATIVE sidecar (Container.Native) is only considered started, so the main container only launches, once it does. Unlike the other two paths it has no default: only the container knows what "started" means. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:MaxLength=2048 +kubebuilder:validation:Pattern=`^/.*$`

tcp.description: TCP probes with a TCP connect instead of an HTTP GET. A TCP probe sets no paths. +optional

initialDelaySeconds.description: InitialDelaySeconds is the READINESS initial delay. Default 0: readiness is cheap and never restarts, so there is nothing to wait for. +optional +kubebuilder:default=0 +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=0

periodSeconds.description: PeriodSeconds is the READINESS period. Default 5. +optional +kubebuilder:default=5 +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=1

timeoutSeconds.description: TimeoutSeconds is the per-attempt timeout, for both probes. Default 3, NOT 2. serverkit's readiness handler has a 2s deadline of its own, so a 2s probe timeout would race it and report the handler's slow-but-correct "not ready" as a probe timeout. +optional +kubebuilder:default=3 +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=1

failureThreshold.description: FailureThreshold is how many consecutive READINESS failures take a replica out of the endpoints. Default 3. +optional +kubebuilder:default=3 +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=1

not_activity.description: NotActivity and ExcludeUsersWith are the user-activity rules (obsquery.Activity).

RemoteBuild.description: RemoteBuild mirrors the kcl/schema.k RemoteBuild — an image built by a HOSTED build service rather than on the machine running `forge build`.

RemoteBuildSource.description: RemoteBuildSource mirrors the kcl/schema.k GitSource as it appears inside a RemoteBuild — the repo+ref pin the build is performed against.

RenderedGeneratedSecret.description: RenderedGeneratedSecret is a rendered forge.GeneratedSecret. The render emits the schema defaults for the parameters of kinds the entry is not, so the projection keeps only the ones its kind reads.

RenderedSecretEntity.description: RenderedSecretEntity mirrors the kcl/schema.k RenderedSecret — one k8s Secret forge renders from declared sources. Keys maps each in-Secret key to its value source.

cluster.description: Cluster / Namespace are the EXPLICIT placement (kubectl context + namespace). Always set for a Bundle.rendered_secrets entry. On a RenderedSecrets provider entry an empty Cluster means "infer": land in each cluster whose services reference it by secret_ref.

RenderedSecretKeyEntity.description: RenderedSecretKeyEntity mirrors the kcl/schema.k RenderedSecretKey. From is "dotenv" (read .env.<env> at Key) or "literal" (inline Value, dev/e2e only). A "dotenv" key carries no Value; a "literal" key carries no dotenv Key.

RenderedStore.description: RenderedStore is a rendered store kind. Type is the store's discriminator ("hosted", "openbao", "gcpsm").

Resources.description: Resources is a workload's compute request and limit, in NEUTRAL units: CPU in millicores, memory in BYTES.

cpuLimitMillicores.description: Unset means equal to the CPU request. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=1

memoryLimitBytes.description: Unset means equal to the memory request. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=1

RouteHealthCheckEntity.description: RouteHealthCheckEntity mirrors kcl/schema.k's RouteHealthCheck — an ACTIVE health check. ExpectedStatuses is the field that matters: a token-authed registry answers /v2/ with 401 when healthy, so a default 2xx check would mark every replica down.

RouteOutlierDetectionEntity.description: RouteOutlierDetectionEntity mirrors kcl/schema.k's RouteOutlierDetection — PASSIVE health checking, which ejects an endpoint that is failing real requests.

RouteRetriesEntity.description: RouteRetriesEntity mirrors kcl/schema.k's RouteRetries — how a route retries a failed attempt at its backend. On is Envoy Gateway's closed trigger set (5xx, reset, connect-failure, …).

RouteTrafficEntity.description: RouteTrafficEntity mirrors kcl/schema.k's RouteTraffic — the typed per-route policy that renders ONE Envoy Gateway BackendTrafficPolicy. Timeout is the whole-request timeout (a multi-GB blob upload runs far past Envoy's 15s default).

RuntimeConfigValue.description: RuntimeConfigValue is one entry of a StaticSite's runtime config: EXACTLY ONE of a literal value or a workload URL reference.

workloadURL.description: WorkloadURL resolves to another workload's public URL. +optional

SchemaOnlyDatabaseEntity.description: SchemaOnlyDatabaseEntity is one database declared for its schema only (a bare forge.Database on Bundle.schema_only_databases): nothing runs or is reached for it.

dialect.description: Dialect is the database's SQL dialect: postgres.

migrations.description: Migrations is where its migrations live and which tool applies them.

orm.description: ORM places its generated data layer.

SecretKeyRef.description: SecretKeyRef names one key of a Secret in the workload's own namespace.

optional.description: Optional lets the pod start when the Secret or the key does not exist; the variable is then simply unset. It is what the config projection emits for an OPTIONAL sensitive field, whose absence the app already handles. A required reference to a missing key holds the pod in CreateContainerConfigError, with no application log, which is the right outcome only when the value really is required. +optional

SecretProviderEntity.description: SecretProviderEntity is the parsed bundle-level secret provider declaration. Type is "dotenv" | "external" | "rendered". Path is the dotenv path (dotenv only), resolved relative to the project root by the CLI. Secrets is the declared Secret set (rendered only).

secrets.description: Secrets is populated for Type=="rendered": the explicit Secret declarations (name + per-key source) forge renders + applies per cluster. Empty for dotenv/external.

generate.description: Generate is populated for Type=="file": store key -> how to mint it when absent (FileSecrets.generate). Never set for any other provider.

SecretVolumeSource.description: SecretVolumeSource names a Secret, and optionally which keys to project.

items.description: Items selects keys and their file paths. Unset projects every key as a file named after it. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:MaxItems=64

optional.description: Optional lets the pod start while the Secret does not exist yet; the kubelet fills the volume in once it appears. A Secret the control plane delivers after the first deploy (forge.ControlPlaneSecret) is mounted this way, so a first deploy never waits on it. +optional

ShapeApprovalHook.description: ShapeApprovalHook: before a promotion to this env is written, the hook is asked, with an [ApprovalRequest], and answers an [ApprovalDecision]. Exactly one of URL (an HTTPS endpoint the env's ledger POSTs to: the control plane for an env that has one, forge otherwise) or Argv (a command forge runs, with no shell, for an env without a control plane) is set.

timeout_seconds.description: TimeoutSeconds bounds one ask, 1..60. A hook that has not answered by then is a deny in enforce.

ShapeApprovals.description: ShapeApprovals: Required distinct people must approve a promotion, the requester included. 1 is one-person approval. Approvers are the org members who may approve; more than one required needs at least that many.

ShapeBucket.description: ShapeBucket is one object-storage bucket the env declares (forge.Bucket), as a reader outside the app needs to find it: the control plane's storage browser lists these, and resolves each to a backend by RuntimeKind.

name.description: Name is the forge.Bucket's name: what a BucketRef names it by, and the key a reader looks it up by ([Shape.BucketNamed]).

public_read.description: PublicRead is forge.Bucket.public_read: every object is readable without a signature.

bucket.description: Bucket is the real bucket name, for the runtimes forge does not manage (s3, gcs), resolved: the declared one, else Name. Empty for minio (whose bucket is Name) and hosted (resolved from the ManagedBucket).

endpoint.description: Endpoint is the S3 API's base URL for an s3 bucket (and a gcs bucket that is not on storage.googleapis.com), scheme included. Empty otherwise.

ShapeBundleKinds.description: ShapeBundleKinds narrows, never widens, the mandatory ingest baseline: Allow non-empty means only those kinds; Deny refuses these. `Kind` or `group/Kind`.

ShapeControl.description: ShapeControl is a control with no parameters beyond its mode.

ShapeDataAccess.description: ShapeDataAccess is the env's declared access to its data (forge.DataAccess).

storage.description: Storage is the storage-browser policy when the env declares one that differs from DBQuery; empty means "the same as DBQuery". Read it through [ShapeDataAccess.Resolved], never directly. Omitted when empty, so every shape recorded before the field encodes and hashes as it did; a control plane that predates it refuses the whole shape, so it is a bundle-document feature ([BundleFeatureStorage]).

ShapeDeliveryPolicy.description: ShapeDeliveryPolicy is what an env's releases must prove before they ship, one control per hardening control of the delivery design, each with a mode and its parameters. It is how the control plane learns what to enforce: recorded on every ensure, enforced at record (builder, signature, provenance, SBOM, vulnerabilities, kinds), at promote (approvals, the promotion's signature), at the converger (Flux verification) and at admission (pod images).

health_gate.description: HealthGate is the promotion health gate (forge.HealthGate). Nil is its default — mode enforce, no environments named, so no gate — and is how a policy that declares none encodes, so every shape recorded before the field still hashes as it did. A reader that predates it never sees it: it is the bundle feature [BundleFeatureHealthGate].

required_gates.description: RequiredGates is forge.RequiredGates: the checks a promotion to this env must carry as passed. Nil is its default — enforce, naming nothing, so no requirement — and how a policy that declares none encodes. A reader that predates it never sees it: it is the bundle feature [BundleFeaturePromotionChecks].

approval_hook.description: ApprovalHook is forge.ApprovalHook: the team's own approval system, asked approve / deny / pending before a promotion to this env is written. Nil is no hook. Bundle feature [BundleFeaturePromotionChecks].

ShapeHealthGate.description: ShapeHealthGate: a promotion of release R to this env is admitted only once every env in After has proved R good — the control plane holds a release-health verdict of PASS for its newest promotion of R there (the verdict `forge obs check` reports as exit 0). The order is declared, never inferred: an empty After gates nothing, whatever the mode. `enforce` refuses an unproven promotion unless it carries the recorded override; `audit` admits it and records what enforce would have refused.

ShapeIdentity.description: ShapeIdentity is the env's managed identity as DECLARED (forge.ManagedIdentity): what the control plane's identity reconciler converges an instance to. It records names only — a SMTP password, a seed user's password and a machine user's key are secret NAMES, and every issued value is delivered, never recorded.

name.description: Name names the outputs (forge-identity-<name>) and the declaration.

runtime.description: Runtime is where the instance runs: [IdentityRuntimeHosted] or [IdentityRuntimeHost].

share_with.description: ShareWith is the env of the SAME project that owns the instance this env's applications live in. Empty when this env owns its instance.

project_name.description: ProjectName is the identity project's name. Empty means the env's project; an adopted instance keeps its legacy name here.

public.description: Public is the declaration's own claim that the instance needs a public route (hosted login, an explicit public = True). The control plane also raises it for a consumer outside the platform network, which only it can see.

domain.description: Domain is a custom issuer domain (login.acme.com), instead of the assigned <slug>.reliantidentity.com.

deliveries.description: Deliveries are the Secrets the control plane writes this identity's outputs into on a connected cluster. Each is ALSO an entry of Shape.ControlPlaneSecrets, which is how the existing delivery path sees it; this list says which of those entries are the identity's.

managed_secrets.description: ManagedSecrets are the reserved managed-secret names the control plane writes the outputs under for HOSTED consumers. They are not the env's secrets: nobody sets them.

owners.description: Owners are seeded on every pass (created email-verified, granted OwnerRole, invited while credential-less). ADDITIVE AND STICKY: an address removed here is never revoked. Lower-cased.

owner_role.description: OwnerRole is set only when Owners is non-empty.

signup.description: Signup is who may create an account. Nil = [IdentitySignupInvite].

methods.description: Methods are the first-factor methods offered ([IdentityMethodPassword], ...). When the declaration does not [ShapeIdentity.DeclaresLoginPolicy] it is nil, meaning [password] and "leave the login policy alone". When it does, the render always lists them, so nil there means none (social sign-in only). Read it through [ShapeIdentity.SignInMethods].

passkey_rp_id.description: PasskeyRPID is the WebAuthn relying-party id. Empty = the host of the app's sign-in origin.

email.description: Email is how the instance's mail is addressed. Nil = {delivery: platform}.

dev_mail.description: DevMail is the mailpit HostInfra a host-run instance's mail goes to. Host runtime only.

ShapeIdentityApplication.description: ShapeIdentityApplication is one OIDC application registered in the instance.

workload.description: Workload is the broker: the workload that runs the sign-in endpoint.

login_uri.description: LoginURI is the declared literal override. Empty means the control plane derives it from the env's frontend.

ShapeIdentityConsumer.description: ShapeIdentityConsumer is one workload whose typed config the identity's outputs fill.

application.description: Application is the application this consumer brokers for. Empty for a consumer that only validates tokens.

fields.description: Fields maps an output ([IdentityOutputs]) to the config field it fills when that is not the standard one (the 20%: an app that validates two issuers).

deliver_only.description: DeliverOnly says the control plane delivers this consumer's Secrets but forge projects nothing into the workload: it still reads its own config.

omit.description: Omit lists outputs ([IdentityOmittableOutputs]) forge does not project into the workload, for an app whose config has no field for them. The Secrets still carry them.

ShapeIdentityDelivery.description: ShapeIdentityDelivery names one Secret of Shape.ControlPlaneSecrets as belonging to the identity.

ShapeIdentityEmail.description: ShapeIdentityEmail is how the instance's mail is addressed.

delivery.description: Delivery is [IdentityMailPlatform] or [IdentityMailNone]. Ignored when smtp is declared.

from_name.description: FromName is the From display name. Empty = the project.

from_local.description: FromLocal is the From local part; the domain is assigned by the platform. Empty with smtp, whose sender is the From.

ShapeIdentityKeySecret.description: ShapeIdentityKeySecret is a delivery destination: a Secret on a connected cluster.

ShapeIdentityLogin.description: ShapeIdentityLogin is how users sign in.

ShapeIdentityMachineUser.description: ShapeIdentityMachineUser is a non-human account whose key is delivered.

key_secret.description: KeySecret is where its key is delivered. Required for a hosted instance; a host-run one keeps the key in the env's secret store.

ShapeIdentityRole.description: ShapeIdentityRole is one role of the identity project.

members.description: Members are the declared members' emails. Only with MembersFrom declared.

ShapeIdentitySMTP.description: ShapeIdentitySMTP is a bring-your-own mail relay. PasswordSecret is a managed-secret NAME.

ShapeIdentitySeedUser.description: ShapeIdentitySeedUser is a user created in a local or ephemeral env. PasswordSecret is a secret NAME.

ShapeIdentitySignup.description: ShapeIdentitySignup is who may create an account from the sign-in screen.

domains.description: Domains are the lower-case DNS names a domain-mode signup's VERIFIED address must be in. A subdomain matches only if listed itself.

role.description: Role is granted to a self-signed-up account once verified. Empty = none.

ShapeIdentitySocial.description: ShapeIdentitySocial is one social identity provider, with the app's own OAuth client. The client secret (and a secret client id) are managed-secret NAMES: only the identity reconciler reads them, and no workload is handed them.

client_id.description: ClientID is the literal client id, OR ClientIDSecret names it.

client_secret_secret.description: ClientSecretSecret names the client secret, always.

ShapePreview.description: ShapePreview is Shape.Preview: the env is a preview instance of the env Of, to be deleted once ExpiresAt (RFC 3339, UTC) has passed. Source says what it previews ("pr-123", "branch feat/x"), for a human reading a list.

ShapeReleaseHealth.description: ShapeReleaseHealth is the env's release-health policy (forge.ReleaseHealth): the thresholds a promotion is judged by, and which findings fail it rather than warn. The control plane's GetReleaseHealth reads it from the env's recorded shape, so the console, the CLI and alerting judge a release by the one declaration.

window_seconds.description: WindowSeconds is the length of each of the two windows compared: before the promotion and after it.

min_requests.description: MinRequests is the after-window traffic below which a service is not judged (the verdict is inconclusive, not a pass).

max_error_rate_increase.description: MaxErrorRateIncrease is the absolute error-rate rise, as a fraction (0.01 = one percentage point), above which error_rate fires.

max_p95_ratio.description: MaxP95Ratio is the after/before p95 ratio above which latency fires.

new_issue_min_events.description: NewIssueMinEvents is the events a new issue needs before it counts.

fail_on.description: FailOn are the finding codes that fail a release; the rest warn. Sorted, no duplicates.

require_baseline.description: RequireBaseline is how many services the release needs a before window of MinRequests for: BaselineAny, BaselineEvery or BaselineNone. Empty means BaselineAny, and is how the default is recorded, so a shape that keeps it encodes as it did before the field (a reader that predates it is sent none: BundleFeatureReleaseHealthBaseline).

ShapeRequiredGates.description: ShapeRequiredGates: a promotion to this env is admitted only when it carries a gate of every name in Names, each with status passed (`forge env deploy --gate name=e2e,status=passed`, or a forge `--gate-json` document). A gate that is missing refuses the promotion `required_gate_missing`; one carried as failed, error or skipped refuses it `required_gate_failed`. An empty Names requires nothing, whatever the mode, so naming a gate is the opt-in. `audit` admits and records what enforce would have refused.

ShapeSigning.description: ShapeSigning: images and the bundle are signed. Key is the key model; KeyRef is a customer key's PUBLIC reference (never key material); OIDCIssuer and OIDCSubject name the identity a keyless signature must come from.

ShapeTrustedBuilder.description: ShapeTrustedBuilder: only artifacts built by the platform's builder for the org, or by one of Builders (`<kind>:<id>`), are eligible.

ShapeUptimeCheck.description: ShapeUptimeCheck is one outside-in HTTP check of an env: what to request, how often, and what counts as up. The control plane's prober reads it from the env's recorded shape, so the declaration is the only place a check lives.

name.description: Name is unique within the env. It tags every metric the prober writes.

url.description: URL is the absolute address to request. Empty exactly when Target is set.

target.description: Target is a hosted frontend's or workload's name: the control plane resolves its platform hostname, and requests Path on it.

path.description: Path is requested on Target's hostname ("/" when empty). Not valid with URL.

interval_seconds.description: IntervalSeconds and TimeoutSeconds schedule the check.

expect_status.description: ExpectStatus lists the statuses that mean up: "200", or a class ("2xx"). Empty means [DefaultUptimeExpectStatus].

expect_body.description: ExpectBody is a substring the response body must contain. Empty means the body is not read. Needs Method GET.

ShapeVulnExempt.description: ShapeVulnExempt is one accepted advisory: time-boxed, with its reason.

ShapeVulnGate.description: ShapeVulnGate: a finding blocks when it is KEV-listed (BlockKEV), or when its severity is at or above BlockSeverity and, with FixableOnly, a fixed version exists. A non-blocking finding at or above WarnSeverity is warned.

ShellBuild.description: ShellBuild mirrors the kcl/schema.k ShellBuild — the SINGLE shell escape hatch: a verbatim `sh -c` build command that owns the whole build (and any push).

built_images.description: BuiltImages maps an env var the command reads to the workload whose built image it carries. The build runs each named workload first and sets the var to the `<repository>@sha256:<digest>` it pushed — see externalBuildGraph.

inputs.description: Inputs are the globs (relative to the resolved cwd) naming the files the command reads. Declared, they let a build whose fingerprint and pushed image are unchanged be skipped — see build_external_inputs.go.

StatefulSetResizeOutput.description: StatefulSetResizeOutput is `output.statefulset_resize`: the tuning of the Job that converges a StatefulSet whose declared volume grew. Present only when the env declares Bundle.statefulset_resize.

disabled.description: Disabled opts the env out of the resize Job.

image.description: Image replaces the Job's default image ("" for the default).

release_owner.description: ReleaseOwner is the release-inputs owner the Job's image is pinned by.

StaticSiteCDN.description: StaticSiteCDN is the CDN in front of a bucket and the per-deploy invalidation policy. Absent (nil) means the bucket is served directly and a deploy invalidates nothing.

StoreSourceEntity.description: StoreSourceEntity is a rendered forge.StoreSource: release's own record (store, data, generate, pin, immutable) plus the fields the secret commands read that the release shape does not carry.

templates.description: Templates are the Secret keys ESO renders from the fetched data.

creation_policy.description: CreationPolicy is "Orphan" or "Merge": whether ESO rebuilds the Secret's data from the declared keys only, or merges into what is there.

secret_type.description: SecretType is the Kubernetes Secret type ESO gives the synced Secret when it is not Opaque ("kubernetes.io/basic-auth").

labels.description: Labels are put on the synced Secret.

shadow.description: Shadow syncs into <name>-eso-shadow instead of <name> (migration step 2).

cluster.description: Cluster is the kubectl context the Secret lands on when the source names one; empty means the env's primary cluster.

Toleration.description: Toleration lets the workload's pods schedule onto nodes with a matching taint. It is a local mirror of core/v1 Toleration, for the same reasons as PolicyRule: the schema is closed and self-contained.

key.description: Key is the taint key. Empty, with operator Exists, tolerates every taint. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:MaxLength=316

operator.description: Operator is Exists or Equal. Unset means Equal (Kubernetes' default). +optional

value.description: Value is the taint value to match, for operator Equal. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:MaxLength=63

effect.description: Effect is the taint effect to match. Unset matches every effect. +optional

tolerationSeconds.description: TolerationSeconds bounds how long a NoExecute taint is tolerated before eviction. Unset means forever. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=0

Volume.description: Volume is one pod volume and its mount into the MAIN container.

name.description: Name is the volume name, unique within the pod. +kubebuilder:validation:MinLength=1 +kubebuilder:validation:MaxLength=63 +kubebuilder:validation:Pattern=`^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$`

mountPath.description: MountPath is the absolute path the volume mounts at in the main container. +kubebuilder:validation:MinLength=1 +kubebuilder:validation:MaxLength=4096 +kubebuilder:validation:Pattern=`^/.*$`

readOnly.description: ReadOnly mounts the volume read-only. Secret and ConfigMap volumes are conventionally read-only; an emptyDir is usually writable scratch. +optional

source.description: Source is where the volume's content comes from: exactly one kind.

VolumeSource.description: VolumeSource is exactly one of the four closed volume sources.

secret.description: Secret projects a Secret in the workload's namespace as files. +optional

configMap.description: ConfigMap projects a ConfigMap in the workload's namespace as files. +optional

emptyDir.description: EmptyDir is pod-lifetime scratch space, which is the way to give a workload a writable path under forge's read-only root filesystem. +optional

pvc.description: PVC mounts an EXISTING PersistentVolumeClaim. For storage forge provisions, use WorkloadSpec.StorageGiB. +optional

WorkloadSpec.description: WorkloadSpec is everything that runs, as ONE declaration (ADR 0002).

kind.description: Kind is how the workload runs. Default service. +optional +kubebuilder:default=service

image.description: Image is the container image, resolved by the lowering (the build output, or an author-named third-party image). ProfileRestricted also requires it to be registry-qualified and pinned, because the platform pulls it from a registry the hosted user does not control. A cluster the author operates may run a locally imported bare name. +kubebuilder:validation:MinLength=1 +kubebuilder:validation:MaxLength=500

command.description: Command overrides the image's entrypoint. Rare: a forge-built project binary is selected by Args, not by replacing the entrypoint. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:MaxItems=64 +kubebuilder:validation:items:MaxLength=4096

args.description: Args are the entrypoint's arguments, typically the project binary's subcommand. The host runtime derives its command from the build plus these same args, so they are stated once for every runtime. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:MaxItems=64 +kubebuilder:validation:items:MaxLength=4096

replicas.description: Replicas is the pod count for a service, worker or operator. Default 1. A batch kind's concurrency belongs to its Job or CronJob, and a tool is never scheduled, so neither may set more than one. +optional +kubebuilder:default=1 +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=1

resources.description: Resources is the compute request and limit. Omitted means the entry shape (250m / 1 GiB). +optional

env.description: Env is the container environment. There is no portable entry-count limit: exec limits apply to the resolved environment and arguments in bytes, including values supplied by secret references at runtime. +optional +listType=map +listMapKey=name

ports.description: Ports are the ports the container listens on. A service's ports are all on its ClusterIP Service. An operator's and a worker's are container ports only, because nothing resolves them by name. +optional +listType=map +listMapKey=name +kubebuilder:validation:MaxItems=16

probes.description: Probes are the readiness and liveness probes. Omitted means the policy in EffectiveProbes: TCP on the first port for a service that declares ports, and none for anything else. The lowering writes HTTP /readyz + /healthz explicitly for a service forge built, and for a forge-built operator that declares ports. +optional

storageGiB.description: StorageGiB provisions a ReadWriteOnce PersistentVolumeClaim of this many GiB, mounted at /data. Zero means stateless.

schedule.description: Schedule is a cron's schedule: a 5-field cron expression or one of @hourly, @daily, @weekly, @monthly, @yearly. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:MaxLength=128

before.description: Before names the workloads that must not start until this job exits 0, or [BeforeAll] for every workload in the environment. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:MaxItems=64

deployPhase.description: DeployPhase places a standalone job in the deploy. Unset means pre-rollout (EffectiveDeployPhase). There is no default marker: a static default would be stamped on every kind, and Validate would then refuse the CR it was handed. +optional

namespacedRBAC.description: NamespacedRBAC grants a Role + RoleBinding in the workload's own namespace, in addition to forge's default config-read rules. The Role is rendered whenever the workload has ANY RBAC (either tier, or kind operator); with none, there is no Role at all and no mounted token. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:MaxItems=64

clusterRBAC.description: ClusterRBAC grants a ClusterRole + ClusterRoleBinding.
