Any scheduled kind may declare it (Full profile only): an operator watches its CRDs cluster-wide, and a service may legitimately resolve resources across namespaces (a proxy routing to per-workspace objects) without being a controller. It ADDS to the namespaced Role rather than replacing it: the ClusterRole carries only cluster-scoped intent (these rules, and an operator's CRD-derived rules), while the config-read defaults and an operator's leader-election lease stay in the namespaced Role. Both bind the one ServiceAccount, so NamespacedRBAC and ClusterRBAC may be declared together, each at its own scope. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:MaxItems=64

crds.description: CRDs are the custom resource kinds an operator's manager owns. May be empty: an operator that owns none yet, or reconciles built-in kinds. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:MaxItems=64 +kubebuilder:validation:items:Pattern=`^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$`

group.description: Group is the API group of an operator's CRDs. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:MaxLength=253 +kubebuilder:validation:Pattern=`^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*$`

version.description: Version is the API version of an operator's CRDs. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:MaxLength=63 +kubebuilder:validation:Pattern=`^v[0-9]+((alpha|beta)[0-9]+)?$`

leaderElection.description: LeaderElection turns an operator's leader election on or off. Unset means on (EffectiveLeaderElection). A pointer, with no default marker, because the default is true only for an operator. A static default would stamp it onto every kind. +optional

serviceAccountAnnotations.description: ServiceAccountAnnotations are stamped on the workload's generated ServiceAccount and on no other object. Cloud workload identity is the case it exists for: GKE reads iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account, and EKS reads eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn, off the KSA the pod runs as. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:MaxProperties=32

sidecars.description: Sidecars are additional containers in the workload's pod: a Cloud SQL Auth Proxy, a registry forwarder. They get the same hardened securityContext as the main container. +optional +listType=map +listMapKey=name +kubebuilder:validation:MaxItems=8

volumes.description: Volumes are extra pod volumes, each mounted into the main container. For storage forge provisions, use StorageGiB. +optional +listType=map +listMapKey=name +kubebuilder:validation:MaxItems=32

serviceAccount.description: ServiceAccount names an EXISTING ServiceAccount to run as, instead of the one forge generates. The case is cloud workload identity bound to a ServiceAccount that other infrastructure owns. forge then renders no ServiceAccount, Role or binding for the workload, so this is mutually exclusive with NamespacedRBAC, ClusterRBAC and ServiceAccountAnnotations: each of those describes the generated ServiceAccount, which no longer exists.

nodeSelector.description: NodeSelector constrains the pods to nodes with these labels. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:MaxProperties=32

tolerations.description: Tolerations let the pods schedule onto tainted nodes. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:MaxItems=32

podAnnotations.description: PodAnnotations are stamped on the pod template. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:MaxProperties=64

strategy.description: Strategy is how the Deployment replaces its pods on a rollout.

priorityClassName.description: PriorityClassName names a PriorityClass that ranks these pods against everything else competing for a node: the scheduler places a higher priority pod first, and a preempting class evicts lower priority pods to make room. The case is a workload sharing nodes with pods that already carry a class — without one it is priority 0 and loses every contest, so a rollout's surge pod can be preempted repeatedly and take minutes to land.

enableServiceLinks.description: EnableServiceLinks opts the pods IN to Kubernetes' service links: an env var per Service in the namespace (<NAME>_PORT=tcp://ip:port, <NAME>_SERVICE_HOST, <NAME>_SERVICE_PORT, ...). Unset (false) renders pod.enableServiceLinks: false, because those names are not namespaced to anything: a Service called `temporal` injects TEMPORAL_PORT, which a typed config loader then parses as a port number and the process CrashLoops at boot (reliant's daemon-gateway, 2026-10-21; Zitadel's ZITADEL_PORT before it). Resolve a Service through DNS (<svc>.<namespace>.svc) or an explicit env var instead. Set this only for an image that reads the injected variables. Full profile only. +optional

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: TerminationGracePeriodSeconds overrides the drain-derived grace period (PRE_STOP_DELAY + SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT + 5 from the workload's env). For a process whose shutdown budget is not expressed in those env vars: a Temporal worker finishing in-flight activities needs 60s. Full profile only. 0 is honoured (SIGKILL immediately). +optional +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=0 +kubebuilder:validation:Maximum=3600

preStopSeconds.description: PreStopSeconds is how long a stopping pod keeps running before it is sent SIGTERM, so the load balancers routing to it see it leave its Service's endpoints first. A forge-built server needs none: on SIGTERM it fails /readyz and keeps serving for PRE_STOP_DELAY itself. An image forge did not build (a DockerBuild, a third-party server) reads neither knob and closes its listener while it is still routed, so requests reach a dead socket during every rollout. This pauses it instead.

activeDeadlineSeconds.description: ActiveDeadlineSeconds bounds a job or cron run: Kubernetes fails the Job (Job.spec.activeDeadlineSeconds) once it has run this long, and the host runtime kills the process. A one-shot that can hang would otherwise block a deploy or `forge env up` forever. Allowed under every profile: a timeout only ever shortens what runs. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=1

successfulJobsHistoryLimit.description: SuccessfulJobsHistoryLimit and FailedJobsHistoryLimit are how many finished Jobs a cron keeps (CronJob.spec.successfulJobsHistoryLimit / failedJobsHistoryLimit). Unset keeps Kubernetes' defaults, 3 and 1; 0 keeps none. Cron only. Allowed under every profile: they only ever remove finished objects. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=0 +kubebuilder:validation:Maximum=100

ttlSecondsAfterFinished.description: TTLSecondsAfterFinished deletes each of a cron's Jobs, with its pods, this long after it finishes (Job.spec.ttlSecondsAfterFinished). The history limits bound HOW MANY finished Jobs stay; this bounds how LONG, so a failure stays inspectable for a while and is not kept forever by a later run that succeeded. Cron only: a kind=job Workload is applied by every release, so expiring its Job would make the next apply run it again. Allowed under every profile. +optional +kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=0

securityContext.description: SecurityContext loosens forge's pod identity defaults for an image that needs it: a Next.js standalone image that runs as uid 1000 and writes into its own tree. Full profile only. It is deliberately NOT a Kubernetes securityContext passthrough: no privileged, no capabilities, no host namespaces, and runAsNonRoot stays forced, so every pod is still Pod Security `restricted`. +optional

WorkloadURLRef.description: WorkloadURLRef names a workload, in the same environment, whose public URL is the value. Resolution is scoped by construction: the name carries no org, env or namespace component, so a reference can only ever reach a sibling workload.

name.description: Name is the target workload's name (its metadata.name). +kubebuilder:validation:MinLength=1 +kubebuilder:validation:MaxLength=63 +kubebuilder:validation:Pattern=`^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$`

deliveryUnitRaw.description: deliveryUnitRaw is one `output.delivery_units[]` entry. After is a pointer-ish slice on purpose: null (unset) means "after the default unit", an empty list means "waits for nothing", and the two must not be conflated.

kclWorkloadRaw.description: kclWorkloadRaw is one `output.workloads[]` entry before dispatch.

build_image.description: BuildImage is the build identity: Image plus the tag the workload pins, if any. Emitted for every built workload on every runtime.

delivery_unit.description: DeliveryUnit is the unit the workload's objects are delivered in.

manifestOwner.description: KCLEntities is the typed view of the JSON contract the KCL deploy module emits: `output = forge.render(bundle)` (P2 map §9 is normative).
